purpose: Record bounded corrected source re-extractions for the 10 selected C2-LT-B1 source-resolution candidates before any reviewed artifact or model admission decision.

scope.extractionLimit: This register records corrected source-context extraction only; it does not itself create reviewed artifacts or authorize model admission.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Corrects the prior sepsis row to the SCCM Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guidelines page for the 2026 International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Current adult SSC route candidate as of 2026-07-02; it updates the 2021 SSC guideline and should be used as currentness anchor while the 2021 PMC/PubMed guideline remains prior-version lineage.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating adult sepsis and septic shock as a time-critical continuity domain spanning hospital, immediate prehospital and immediate post-hospital management, sepsis screening, treatment procedures and antimicrobial stewardship. The SCCM page states the 2026 adult guideline includes 129 statements, 46 new statements and more definitive recommendations.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints or variables include sepsis screening coverage, time-to-recognition, standard operating procedure availability, antimicrobial initiation/de-escalation route, organ dysfunction trajectory, shock transition, ICU/hospital mortality, ARDS/mechanical ventilation route and post-hospital continuity.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Adult patients with sepsis or septic shock in hospital, immediate prehospital and immediate post-hospital settings. Pediatric sepsis, individualized treatment decisions and local protocol details remain outside this row.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: infection-triggered dysregulated host response can create organ dysfunction and shock; earlier recognition, structured procedures, responsible antimicrobial use and organ-support pathways are potential hazard-transition variables.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline recommendations aggregate heterogeneous evidence and implementation settings. Access to diagnostics, antibiotics, ICU capacity, staffing, antimicrobial resistance patterns and local protocol fidelity can strongly limit transferability.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as guideline-route, endpoint and source-currentness vocabulary for adult sepsis. Do not use as a calibrated effect size, individual treatment pathway or proof that any sepsis intervention improves Human Infra model outcomes.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if later extraction cannot bind a specific recommendation or endpoint to a recommendation class, comparator or setting.
Downgrade if the row is reused for pediatric sepsis, outpatient infection management or individual antibiotic decisions.
Block model use if implementation capacity, antimicrobial resistance or ICU access constraints are ignored.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: corrected current source identity, route vocabulary and candidate endpoint definition only

sourceEvidenceTrace.finding: SCCM identifies the adult Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 guideline, its adult sepsis/septic shock scope, update relationship to 2021 and recommendation-count/currentness signals.

extractedRows.nextAction: Send to independent fresh review as current adult sepsis guideline extraction; create artifacts only if review confirms bounded source use.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Surviving sepsis campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Preserves the 2021 SSC adult guideline as prior-version bibliographic and PMC lineage for the corrected sepsis row, not as the current 2026 anchor.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Prior version relative to SCCM 2026 adult guideline. It remains useful for lineage and for extracting historically published adult sepsis route concepts only when marked as previous-version.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports prior-version context that sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to infection; early identification and appropriate initial-hour management are guideline concerns; hospitals and systems are recommended to use performance improvement programs, screening for high-risk acutely ill patients and standard operating procedures.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate lineage endpoints include prior-version sepsis screening program, standard operating procedure presence, early treatment route, organ dysfunction and mortality/fatality burden signals.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Adult hospital patients with sepsis or septic shock under the 2021 guideline scope. Use as lineage/context when comparing 2021 to 2026 guideline updates.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: dysregulated infection response creates organ dysfunction; early recognition and standardized processes can define hazard-detection and transition variables.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: The guideline is superseded or updated by the 2026 SCCM page for currentness. Its use should not erase later recommendations, newer evidence or changed implementation contexts.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as prior-version lineage and background route context. Do not promote as current adult sepsis guidance when the 2026 source is available.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if this row is cited as current 2026 guidance.
Downgrade if prior-version statements are used without checking whether the 2026 guideline changed them.
Block direct artifact promotion unless independent review confirms whether the artifact is lineage-only or source-card eligible.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: prior-version lineage and source-currentness boundary only

sourceEvidenceTrace.finding: PubMed indexes the 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline, journal, date, DOI and PMC full-text linkage.
PMC full text exposes the adult sepsis/septic shock scope, sepsis definition, early identification framing and screening/treatment procedure recommendations.

extractedRows.nextAction: Use only as prior-version lineage unless independent review explicitly promotes a bounded lineage artifact.

extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Corrects the blocked anaphylaxis row to the 2023 practice parameter update indexed in PubMed.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Practice parameter update published in Annals of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology in 2024 and focused on seven areas with new evidence and recommendations. It should be paired with source-specific review before being treated as current clinical guidance.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating anaphylaxis as an emergency continuity domain involving revised diagnostic criteria, pattern definition, serum tryptase for diagnosis/underlying mast-cell disorders, age-specific pediatric presentation, setting-specific prevention/treatment, epinephrine autoinjector counseling and post-event diagnostic evaluation.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include recognition criteria, serum tryptase measurement route, epinephrine autoinjector availability/training, durable response after epinephrine, EMS activation pathway, recurrent idiopathic or insect-sting anaphylaxis evaluation and perioperative re-exposure planning.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People at risk of or experiencing anaphylaxis across community, pediatric, adult, insect-sting, idiopathic and perioperative settings. This row does not provide individual emergency instructions.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: rapid systemic allergic reaction can create acute airway, circulatory or multisystem failure; recognition, epinephrine access/training, diagnostic workup and specialist evaluation are route variables for continuity protection.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: PubMed abstract supports high-level practice-parameter scope but not all recommendation details, evidence grades or local device availability. Full-text and guideline-body review remain required before artifact promotion.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as emergency-domain variable vocabulary and source identity. Do not use for individual anaphylaxis treatment, device prescription, medication stopping decisions or EMS advice.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if full text cannot confirm the exact recommendation and evidence boundary.
Downgrade if autoinjector or EMS claims are generalized across all patients without context.
Block if the row is used as individual emergency instructions.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: bounded variable and route vocabulary after independent review only

sourceEvidenceTrace.finding: PubMed abstract states the 2023 practice parameter update covers seven new-evidence areas, revised diagnostic criteria, tryptase, pediatric features, community settings, epinephrine autoinjector counseling and post-event evaluation topics.

extractedRows.nextAction: Fresh-review the full practice parameter before creating endpoint or uncertainty artifacts.

extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Adds WAO 2020 guidance as open full-text anaphylaxis guidance context for the corrected anaphylaxis row.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Open guidance published in 2020; useful as accessible global guidance context, but later 2023 practice parameter must be considered for newer evidence and recommendations.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating anaphylaxis as severe acute systemic allergic reaction requiring guidance dissemination; intramuscular epinephrine/adrenaline remains first-line treatment; after anaphylaxis, referral to a specialist for cause assessment, recurrence prevention and self-management education is recommended; epinephrine autoinjector availability and affordability are access constraints.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include IM epinephrine first-line route, specialist referral after event, recurrence-prevention education, self-management capacity, epinephrine autoinjector availability/affordability and country-level access constraints.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Global patients and clinicians dealing with anaphylaxis emergencies; source includes health-system and access considerations, not individual emergency protocols.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: systemic allergic reaction creates acute emergency risk; rapid first-line treatment, post-event referral, education and access to autoinjectors affect continuity through recognition and response capacity.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guidance availability and autoinjector affordability vary by country. Later practice parameters may update specific recommendations. Full text should be reviewed for formal recommendation strength before artifacts are promoted.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as global guidance, access-barrier and emergency-response vocabulary. Do not convert into individual treatment, prescription or emergency dispatch advice.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if the row omits country-level autoinjector availability and affordability constraints.
Downgrade if WAO 2020 is treated as newer than the 2023 practice parameter.
Block if source is used for individual emergency medical instructions.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: global context and access-barrier variables after independent review only

extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Normalizes the blocked stroke row to the NINDS stroke health-information route and its stroke-overview subpage discovered through indexed official search results.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Official NIH/NINDS patient-education route. Direct automated fetch returned 403 during this run, so extraction is limited to official indexed page snippets and should be rechecked manually before artifact promotion.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports only high-level stroke-domain framing: stroke is a medical emergency caused by blocked or burst blood flow to the brain; earlier treatment can reduce disability and save lives; NINDS organizes stroke information around warning signs, prevention, assessment, treatment, recovery and research.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include stroke recognition route, time-to-treatment, emergency activation, brain perfusion interruption, disability outcome, recovery/rehabilitation route and prevention risk-factor route.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: General public, patients, caregivers and health-professional information route for stroke education. Not a clinical guideline or individual diagnosis/treatment source.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: interruption or bleeding in cerebral blood supply can rapidly injure brain cells; timelier recognition and treatment are continuity-relevant because disability and death risks depend on time and severity.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Search-index extraction is weaker than direct source-context reading. The row must stay downgraded until official page content is manually or technically accessible and exact text, dates and subpage boundaries are checked.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as a public-education route and high-level stroke continuity vocabulary. Do not use as an acute stroke guideline, treatment eligibility source or calibrated risk source.
downgradeTriggers: Keep downgraded if the NINDS page remains inaccessible for direct source-context review.
Downgrade if public-education text is used as professional guideline evidence.
Block model use if no independent review confirms warning-sign, treatment and recovery subpage boundaries.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: high-level public-education route only, no artifact promotion before direct-context review

sourceEvidenceTrace.finding: Official indexed NINDS stroke-overview result states stroke is a serious emergency involving blocked or burst brain blood flow, with earlier treatment reducing disability and saving lives.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Corrects the acute ischemic stroke row to the AHA/ASA 2026 guideline page and PubMed-indexed Stroke guideline.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: The 2026 AIS guideline replaces the 2018 acute ischemic stroke guideline and 2019 update; PubMed abstract reports literature through December 2024 plus selected high-impact studies through March 2025.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating acute ischemic stroke as a time-critical continuity domain from prehospital evaluation through acute treatment, early in-hospital complication management and early secondary prevention. AHA page highlights mobile stroke units, EMS triage, tenecteplase within 4.5 hours, broader endovascular thrombectomy eligibility and first pediatric AIS recommendations.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include EMS triage route, mobile stroke unit availability, time-to-thrombolysis, thrombolytic choice/eligibility, endovascular thrombectomy eligibility, hyperglycemia management, dysphagia management, pediatric AIS route and early secondary prevention initiation.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Patients with acute ischemic stroke across prehospital, emergency, acute treatment and early inpatient settings; audience includes prehospital professionals, physicians, allied health professionals and administrators.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: ischemic interruption of cerebral perfusion creates time-sensitive tissue-risk; thrombolysis, thrombectomy, supportive management and early prevention define transition variables for survival and functional outcome pathways.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline recommendations depend on eligibility, imaging, timing, contraindications, local stroke-system capacity and pediatric/adult differences. PubMed abstract and page summaries do not replace full guideline extraction.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as acute stroke guideline route and endpoint vocabulary. Do not use for individual thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility, dosing, emergency advice or calibrated Human Infra effect size.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if full guideline review cannot bind a variable to a recommendation section, eligibility condition or care setting.
Downgrade if ischemic stroke guidance is transferred to hemorrhagic stroke.
Block model use if time-window, imaging, contraindication or local-system capacity constraints are omitted.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: bounded acute-stroke endpoint and pathway vocabulary after independent review only

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Fertility Preservation in People With Cancer: ASCO Guideline Update
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Corrects the fertility-preservation row to the 2025 ASCO guideline update indexed in PubMed.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: ASCO guideline update published in Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2025; PubMed abstract states a multidisciplinary panel updated the systematic review and included 166 studies.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating fertility preservation for people with cancer as a future-option continuity domain: reproductive risks should be evaluated and counseled at diagnosis and during survivorship; interested or uncertain patients should be referred to reproductive specialists; fertility preservation should be discussed before cancer-directed therapy; established methods include sperm cryopreservation, embryo/oocyte/ovarian tissue cryopreservation, ovarian transposition and conservative gynecologic surgery with specific experimental/emerging boundaries.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include reproductive-risk counseling timing, specialist referral, pre-treatment fertility preservation discussion, sperm cryopreservation route, oocyte/embryo/ovarian tissue cryostorage route, ovarian transposition, conservative gynecologic surgery, post-treatment FP route, coverage/access advocacy and pediatric assent/guardian consent boundary.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People with cancer at diagnosis, during treatment planning and survivorship; includes adults, pubertal children and selected prepubertal contexts as bounded by the guideline abstract.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: cancer therapy can reduce future reproductive options; timely counseling, referral and cryopreservation/tissue-preservation pathways preserve future choice space rather than directly extending biological lifespan.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: PubMed abstract provides recommendation-level summary but not all evidence grades, contraindications, cancer-specific timing constraints, access/coverage details or long-term outcome data.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as future-choice/fertility-continuity route and endpoint vocabulary. Do not use as individual oncology, reproductive medicine or insurance advice.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if cancer type, treatment urgency, puberty status, experimental status or access constraints are omitted.
Downgrade if fertility preservation is portrayed as guaranteed future fertility.
Block if used for individual reproductive or cancer-treatment decisions.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: bounded future-choice and route vocabulary after independent review only

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Wound Healing Society Clinical Practice Guidelines and Tools
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Corrects the blocked generic wound-healing row to the WHS clinical tools directory, which routes wound-care guidance by wound type and topic.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Directory source exposes foundational guidelines, wound-type guidance and specific diabetic foot ulcer/pressure ulcer AvoMD module and guideline years. It is a routing source, not a single guideline body.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports splitting the skin/wound domain into wound-type-specific source rows. WHS presents core wound-care guideline documents and topic-specific guidance, including diabetic foot ulcer, pressure ulcer, arterial ulcer, venous ulcer and chronic wound resources, with select pressure-ulcer and diabetic-foot-ulcer guidance accessible through AvoMD/EHR routes.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate route variables include wound type, guideline year, clinical module availability, EHR/app accessibility route and guideline topic category. It does not define wound-healing outcomes by itself.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Wound-care clinicians and guideline users across wound-type categories; source is directory-level and must be split before condition-specific artifacts.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Directory mechanism signal: wound-care evidence is organized by wound type and care module rather than one universal wound-healing intervention; Human Infra extraction must preserve wound-type specificity.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Directory pages may link to publisher content, modules and older guideline versions. Exact recommendation text, evidence strength and endpoint definitions require the specific guideline article or module.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as source-routing and wound-type taxonomy. Do not use the directory page as direct evidence for diabetic foot ulcer treatment, pressure injury care or wound outcome effects.
downgradeTriggers: Keep route-only unless a specific wound-type guideline is extracted.
Downgrade if guideline year, wound type or module route is omitted.
Block artifact promotion if directory text is used as clinical recommendation content.
